reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes recurring USDT and real-money rewards through a Telegram channel and asks viewers to subscribe, complete tasks, send proof, and stay active to claim them. It also invites viewers to pursue millionaire-level crypto success and large dollar returns by starting with a small amount. The narration mentions a later Dogecoin downturn, but the reward channel’s payout behavior and typical investment results are not verified.

citations.quote: My team has launched daily money giveaways 🚀 Join our Telegram channel for daily contests with USDT rewards
Subscribe, complete tasks, send proof, and win real money every weekday! Stay active and claim your USDT! 💵 👉https://t.me/ark_sign_game
Crypto Newbies Become MILLIONAIRES | 5 REAL Stories | Crypto for beginners
Rob decided to take a risk and in February 2021 he invested $8,000 in the coin. Three months later Shiba Inu's value increased 1200 times so his fortune reached more than $9 million.
In February 2021, he spent $180,000 to buy Dogecoins. The price of a token at the time was less than half a cent. In just 2 months, the coin had gone up 10 times in price.

opening.argument: The presentation includes meaningful caution against treating crypto as a guaranteed path to wealth. It explicitly describes Dogecoin rising and then falling, including the investor’s failure to cash out before the downturn. It also tells viewers they do not need to begin with large sums or invest all their spare money. Another account says the family recovered its fortune even though that was not their goal, which undercuts a simple promise of profit. Read in context, the millionaire stories are historical examples accompanied by uncertainty and risk, not a guarantee that viewers will reproduce them.

citations.quote: In May 2021, the Dogecoin exchange rate soared to a record high of 70 cents and then started falling again.
Then came the downturn.
And you don't have to start with large sums and invest all your spare money.
although they themselves admit that they did not set themselves such a goal.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reward language does not establish that the video guarantees an investment return. The description presents a separate contest requiring participation steps, while the narration expressly includes a market downturn and warns against investing all available money. The prosecution’s millionaire examples therefore cannot fairly be treated as a promise that every viewer will receive those outcomes.

citations.quote: Subscribe, complete tasks, send proof, and win real money every weekday!
However, the rapid rise of the coin did not cause the investor to want to cash out but in vain.
And you don't have to start with large sums and invest all your spare money.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cautionary lines do not remove the central promotional framing. The title calls these “5 REAL Stories” of beginners becoming millionaires, while the description says viewers can become one of them today and directs them to a USDT giveaway. Mentioning one downturn and advising small starting amounts still leaves viewers with an invitation to pursue extraordinary crypto gains and a linked reward channel.

citations.quote: Crypto Newbies Become MILLIONAIRES | 5 REAL Stories | Crypto for beginners
You can become one of them today.
Join our Telegram channel for daily contests with USDT rewards

opening.argument: The material is structured as explanatory education: it walks through multiple examples, describes how people researched coins or built mining operations, and closes by offering detailed instructions. The narration says Rob started by reading about cryptocurrencies, explains how the couple solved a coded puzzle, and describes the practical steps used to build mining units. That is commentary and beginner instruction about crypto-related activities, not evidence that the creator is certifying a particular investment or promising a particular viewer a return.

citations.quote: Rob started reading a lot about cryptocurrencies.
In 2018 a 35 year old programmer under the pseudonym Isaac did solve the binary code.
the schoolboy got the idea to create a mining farm, a machine for mining cryptocurrency.
If you want to know how, I have prepared a video with detailed instructions for you.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the subject educational does not make every statement a guarantee, and the supplied narration does not say viewers will duplicate the featured fortunes. It explains past stories and points to instructions, while one story explicitly records a subsequent downturn. The prosecution is inferring a solicitation from educational subject matter rather than identifying a promised outcome.

citations.quote: Then came the downturn.
I have prepared a video with detailed instructions for you.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional closing is precisely what turns the presentation into actionable promotion: viewers are told to subscribe and are offered a way to learn how to start with crypto. The educational format does not cure the accompanying millionaire framing or the linked USDT reward instructions. The cited stories describe exceptional outcomes, but the invitation still encourages viewers to pursue them.

citations.quote: And don't forget to subscribe to our channel to get simple and useful videos and learn this tool better.
Watch the video to the end to find out exactly how to do it.
Crypto Newbies Become MILLIONAIRES | 5 REAL Stories | Crypto for beginners

opening.argument: The clearest concrete offer is framed as an ordinary promotional giveaway: daily contests with USDT rewards in exchange for subscribing, completing tasks, sending proof, and staying active. That is a participation-based promotion, not a stated request to deposit money, transfer crypto, provide credentials, recruit a downline, or accept a guaranteed investment return. The description also says viewers can start with a couple of dollars, but does not specify that any payment is required for the giveaway. Without a demonstrated loss or payout mechanism, suspicion alone does not establish a scam.

citations.quote: My team has launched daily money giveaways 🚀
Join our Telegram channel for daily contests with USDT rewards
Subscribe, complete tasks, send proof, and win real money every weekday!
can start with a couple of dollars

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a linked promotion and participation conditions, but those facts describe the offer rather than proving a fraudulent mechanism. The cited millionaire stories likewise report past crypto price movements, including a downturn, and do not state that viewers must transfer funds to receive a return. The record therefore supports a promotion and crypto content, not the conclusion that the promotion is inherently fraudulent.

citations.quote: Subscribe, complete tasks, send proof, and win real money every weekday!
Then came the downturn.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The promotion is not merely a generic discount: it directs viewers to an external Telegram channel, promises daily real-money or USDT rewards, and conditions claiming them on tasks, proof, and continued activity. The absence of an explicit deposit request does not establish legitimacy. The same description pairs that offer with the message that viewers can become crypto success stories today.
